Sara / Neha — thanks for bringing this over. I reviewed the draft checklist and added a few partner-program specific items. High-level checklist we require for connector certification (summary):

1) Security & Compliance- Network isolation architecture diagram (VPC/VPN options)- TLS in transit + KMS integration for at-rest keys- Data retention and purge behavior documented- SOC 2 artifacts or equivalent (if available)

2) Interoperability & API compatibility- Index schema mapping guidance (pgvector -> Redwood embeddings store)- Backfill/resync procedures for S3 cold-tier objects- SDK compatibility matrix (python/js/java)

3) Performance & Reliability- Latency targets for typical gen/recall flows (p95 < 120ms for small queries)- Bulk ingest throughput and shard sizing recommendations- Retry semantics and idempotency notes

4) Operational readiness- Support SLAs and escalation playbook- Onboarding checklist for customers (MVP integration steps)- Marketing assets: logo (svg), 1-pager, joint case-study template

5) Legal / Commercial- Standard co-sell MSA attachments (redlines allowed)

I attached a short perf-targets doc with our recommended thresholds. If Acme can fill the checklist and provide the network diagram, we can schedule a 60-min technical validation with Karthik's team.

Marissa Cole
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference
[attachment: perf-targets-2026-11.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: certification checklist + partnership collateral

Sara — quick technical notes after skimming your spec:
- Our runtime expects connector responses for vector fetches to be < 50ms additional wall time for warm KV cache lookups; for S3 cold-tier fallthrough we budget an extra 200–500ms depending on batch size. Please document latencies per path.
- Please include a per-query cost estimate and any limits (max vectors per request, payload sizes).
- For pgvector compatibility, confirm support for float32 vs quantized int8 payloads and whether you preserve token alignment in embeddings.
- We will run an interoperability test harness that exercises indexing, query, and failover. Plan: two-hour run with synthetic traffic + one production-like run with a small dataset.

Can Acme propose two week-of dates for the validation run? Also please share the network diagram Marissa requested.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference
